basics.name: Matt Ji
basics.label: Systems & Reliability Engineer
basics.summary: Engineer and risk analyst, ten years where operations meets software. I build the internal infrastructure rather than buying it: one flake declares thirteen NixOS hosts, a task control plane is the operator interface, and the monitoring is a ledger I wrote because no dashboard asked the questions this fleet had. Go and Python services, PostgreSQL, gates in CI and on the host, and a rollback that is a pointer rather than a procedure.

work.name: Bountystash
highlights: Built the internal platform instead of assembling one: a declarative fleet, a task control plane as the single operator interface, a git forge driven through its REST API, and runbooks kept in the same repository as the hosts.

Wrote the telemetry layer by hand: a sentinel records job status, generation age, disk pressure and PSI into a ledger every fifteen minutes and pages on any state that is not ok, because a dashboard nobody reads is not monitoring.
Declared node_exporter on a fleet host and exposed the standard host collector set on :9100, alongside gatus health checks for the services that must answer.
Designed alerts as state changes rather than symptom noise: every repeated manual check became a gate that runs in CI and on the host, so the alert fires once and the fix stays fixed.
Held the wanted state of thirteen Linux hosts in one declaration — GitOps in substance: the repository is the source, each machine pulls from it, and nothing is hand-edited on the target.
Treated a release as one step — build, gate, activate — with rollback as a pointer to the previous generation rather than a restore procedure.

Kept security in the delivery path: SOPS/age secrets per host, an in-house certificate authority with short-lived certificates, nftables default-deny, and dependency and vulnerability work that never leaves the repository.
Administered Linux below the application: systemd units with per-slice memory limits, cgroups, PSI as the saturation signal, and DNS or MTU faults read from tcpdump.
Built Go and Python services with PostgreSQL behind them, including an append-only event log and a terminal UI served from one binary.
Developed an options and hedging algorithm for weather derivatives and advised clients as internal risk manager for a large German energy trader.
Reviewed bug bounty programmes.

projects.name: nixconfig
projects.description: One flake declares thirteen NixOS hosts, an SSH certificate authority, SOPS-encrypted secrets, node_exporter on a fleet host and a taskfile as the operator interface. CI runs the same module gate the machines run.

projects.name: bountystash
projects.description: A Go service that turns a request into an immutable, content-addressed specification. Append-only events, a terminal UI and curl endpoints ship in one binary.

projects.name: kev-time
projects.description: CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue as a time series in plain SVG, legible before a report exists and loadable on a phone during an incident.

projects.name: kelly-svg
projects.description: KEV entries grouped into effort clusters with exposure per cluster, so patch order follows effort and reach instead of catalogue order.

projects.name: Risk Calculation Engine (Swirl Engine)
projects.description: Green's theorem on stochastic polygons: a Go fuzzer generates shapes, a Nushell and Awk pipeline drives the computation, and a Nix environment pins the tools.
highlights: Implemented a shape fuzzer in Go that generates stochastic polygons to load the engine.

projects.name: fibtransponder
projects.description: A Fibonacci-radix state machine that processes a bit stream with bounded work per step. A corpus benchmark falsified the first detector design, so the claim got smaller.

projects.name: Master's Thesis: Weather and Volatility
projects.description: A method for time cross-correlation of wind speed plus neural networks on long-term weather data, to quantify the volatility of solar and wind assets on the grid.

projects.name: Vulnerability operations concept
projects.description: A sample vulnerability programme built from KEV data: exposure table, effort clusters, a 90-day method and a service model.
